title: Lowe's crews rebuild the Pottstown library's children's room at no charge
summary: Employees from four area Lowe's stores, including Oaks, spent the past week laying new floors, painting and building shelves in the basement children's department, a donated renovation valued at about $150,000 through the chain's Hero Project. The room reopens with a celebration at 5:30 p.m. Monday, Nov. 16.
loc: Pottstown Regional Public Library, 500 E. High St., Pottstown

title: Judge lets neighbors join the fight over the Pennhurst data center
summary: A Chester County judge ruled Nov. 10 that the owners of an adjoining 130-acre farm and the group East Vincent Advocacy may help defend the township's rejection of a hyperscale data center on about 125 acres of the former Pennhurst property. Supervisors unanimously denied the plan in May, and it stays denied while the developer's appeal proceeds.
loc: 1205 Commonwealth Drive, East Vincent Township (near Spring City)

title: State sets online meeting on power line across the Schuylkill for proposed Limerick data center
summary: The Department of Environmental Protection will take public comment at a virtual meeting next week on PECO's waterway permit for a transmission line running from East Coventry across the river to Limerick. The line would feed a hyperscale data center proposed on Sanatoga Road, which has not been approved.

title: Phoenixville wound care company wins FDA clearance for new device
summary: Bechtel Medical received 510(k) clearance for Wound VOX, described as the first cleared system to pair negative pressure therapy with topical oxygen for treating wounds. The company designs and makes wound care devices and dressings.

title: Limerick supervisor resigns after 18 years, the board's second departure since September
summary: Kara Shuler announced at Tuesday's meeting that she will step down Jan. 1 because she is moving out of the township. The board has not said how it will pick someone to serve the final year of her term.

title: Phoenixville filmmaker's documentary on domestic violence response screens at the Colonial Nov. 21
summary: Melissa Davey's third feature, Where Fear Ends, follows the Women's Center of Montgomery County from its 1976 start around a kitchen table to a network of seven offices and more than 150 volunteers. The center hosts the 1:30 p.m. screening on Saturday, Nov. 21.

title: Spring-Ford marching band wins its first national championship
summary: The 82-member Golden Rams Marching Band took the USBands Group III Open Class national title at MetLife Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 7, scoring a season-high 94.25 and earning the Best Music caption. It is the first national championship in school history and follows a state title earlier this fall.

title: Historical society opens an exhibit on 22 years of the Firebird Festival
summary: The new show at the Historical Society of the Phoenixville Area museum traces the festival from its 2004 start with design models, videos, fired clay birds and memorabilia, including the 2014 year when vandals burned the bird early and volunteers rebuilt it in days. This year's Firebird Festival is Dec. 12 at Reservoir Park.

title: Private club proposed for residential block of Gay Street goes to zoning board Nov. 18
summary: The 1978 Phoenix Foundation is asking the Zoning Hearing Board for a special exception to run a private club and community center, plus a variance for office use, at 315 Gay St. in the Residential Infill District. The hearing is 7 p.m. Wednesday, Nov. 18, at Borough Hall, and the application can be inspected there.

title: Chicken Salad Chick sets Nov. 18 opening at Providence Town Center
summary: The Southern fast-casual chain's first Philadelphia-area restaurant takes the former Z!Eats space and will seat 55, with free chicken salad for a year promised to the first 100 guests. The local franchise group plans six locations across Montgomery and Chester counties.
loc: 500 Broad St., Providence Town Center, Collegeville
